results.title: Kofi Arko Nokoe commissions Apataim cassava factory to boost local processing
results.content: The Apataim Cassava Factory Project in the Evalue Ajomoro Gwira Constituency has been commissioned, marking a step towards expanding local cassava processing, creating jobs and improving incomes for farmers and processors.

results.title: GHS contains yellow fever outbreak after confirming four cases
results.content: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) says it has contained a yellow fever outbreak recorded between September and the first half of October, after laboratory tests confirmed four cases in parts of the country.

results.title: Ghana will become hostile territory for drug traffickers – Kumadoe
results.content: Security analyst Richard Kumadoe says Ghana is stepping up efforts to disrupt international drug trafficking networks, warning that traffickers who use the country as a transit point risk arrest either locally or at their intended destinations.

results.title: GRASAG-UG, UGSRC warn students against unauthorised protest over accommodation fees
results.content: The Graduate Students’ Association of Ghana (GRASAG-UG) and the University of Ghana Students’ Representative Council (UGSRC) have urged students to stay away from a planned demonstration over accommodation fees, warning that the group organising the protest is not recognised under the university’s governance system.

results.title: Bagbin urges voters to scrutinise campaign promises, resist political propaganda
results.content: The Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, has called on Ghanaians, particularly young people, to take a more critical approach to political campaigns by questioning promises and examining policy proposals before making electoral choices.

results.title: UPSA graduates urged to embrace positive attitudes
results.content: Dr Divine Selase Agbeti, the Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), has urged graduates of the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) to cultivate positive attitudes and commit to continuous learning to succeed in their professional careers.

results.title: ECG announces power outage in parts of Ashanti Region on November 3
results.content: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced a planned power outage in parts of the Ashanti Region on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, to carry out maintenance work to improve electricity service delivery.

results.title: VAST Ghana calls for comprehensive excise tax reforms in 2027-2030 Budget Statement
results.content: The Vision for Accelerated Sustainable Development Ghana (VAST Ghana) has called on the Ministry of Finance to introduce comprehensive excise tax reforms in the 2027-2030 Budget to reduce the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

results.title: ‘No-fees-stress’ policy boosts tertiary education enrollment – SDA College Vice Principal
results.content: The No-Fees-Stress Policy has boosted access to tertiary education, with beneficiaries at the SDA College of Education expressing appreciation to the government for easing the financial burden on students.

results.title: Vice President urges prison officers to respect inmate dignity and support rehabilitation
results.content: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged officers of the Ghana Prisons Service to uphold the dignity of inmates and provide them with opportunities for rehabilitation and successful reintegration into society.

results.title: IMF mission wraps up Ghana PCI review this week as economic targets take centre stage
results.content: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission to Ghana is expected to conclude its first Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI) review engagement this week, with economic targets and the country’s macroeconomic framework likely to dominate the final discussions.

results.title: Petrol drops to GH¢16.38, diesel rises to GH¢18.45 as OMCs adjust pump prices
results.content: Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have begun adjusting pump prices for the first pricing window in November, with petrol prices falling and diesel prices rising.

results.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
results.content: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has put his cabinet ministers and other senior government officials through military training, saying armed forces discipline can help build stronger leaders and advance the country's development.

results.title: China state broadcaster pulls Real Madrid match over Mbappé joke
results.content: China's state broadcaster CCTV did not air a Real Madrid match on Sunday, despite an apology from the club's star striker, Kylian Mbappé, for his "ill-judged" remarks about the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

results.title: ‘Every venue will sell out’ — I will demand $500,000 if I tour with Wizkid – Davido
results.content: Afrobeats singer Davido said a joint tour with Wizkid would sell out venues worldwide, adding that he would demand $500,000 per show.

results.title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years, UN chief says
results.content: The 35-year UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara will end after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate, the UN chief said on Sunday.

results.title: African lenders formally establish $5 billion energy bank
results.content: The African Export-Import Bank and the African Petroleum Producers' Organisation have ​formally established the Africa Energy Bank, ‌according to a statement from Afreximbank on Saturday.

results.title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy in London
results.content: More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.

results.title: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
results.content: Prosecutors in France have launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at police during unrest, French media reported.

results.title: Thousands of jobs at Virgin Media O2 to be cut
results.content: Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff face redundancy risk as the telecoms firm seeks to cut costs amid billions of pounds in debt and tougher competition.

results.title: Samples for two suspected Ebola cases in Nigeria turn out negative
results.content: Health authorities in Nigeria investigating two suspected Ebola cases in the country's northeast region confirmed that samples tested negative after two rounds of testing, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention said on Sunday.

results.title: Oil slips more than 1% as talks continue on ending Iran war
results.content: Oil prices slipped more than 1% on ‌Monday after Iranian and Qatari officials held a third straight day of talks aimed at pushing for a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran.

results.title: I wasted my first earnings from music – Don Jazzy
results.content: Veteran record producer and music executive Michael Collins Ajereh, popularly known as Don Jazzy, revealed that he spent his first major earnings on frivolities rather than investing or using them wisely.

results.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto hack
results.content: Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following a record hack last week.

results.title: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000
results.content: The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic ​Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000, government ‌data showed on Friday, as authorities had yet to find a way to control the country's deadliest ​Ebola epidemic on record.

results.title: Top Swiss court upholds landmark Liberia war crimes ruling
results.content: The top Swiss court on Friday confirmed a ​guilty verdict against a Liberian warlord, ‌upholding his 20-year sentence in the country's first-ever war crimes trial.

results.title: Police forward Ashie Moore case docket to AG for prosecution over alleged theft
results.content: The Ghana Police Service has forwarded the case docket involving Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC), Emmanuel Nii Ashie Moore, to the Attorney-General's Department for prosecution over allegations of stealing from a Singaporean businessman. The forwarding of the docket, with a covering letter dated October 28, 2026, marks a new development in a case that has been under police investigation since 2025, and in which the Attorney-General's Department had, as far back as March 16, 2026, advised that Mr Ashie Moore be prosecuted. Ashie Moore, on the other hand, has vehemently denied any wrongdoing, insisting that the allegations constitute a smear campaign against his political acumen.

results.title: OPEC+ keeps December oil output targets steady ahead of tougher call for 2027
results.content: OPEC+ oil-producing countries kept December production targets steady on Sunday, confirming expectations that the group will not make further policy adjustments until next year, as it continues to struggle with export disruptions from the Iran war.

results.title: Tilly Akua Nipaa appointed Communications Director of RANA
results.content: The Rights Accountability Network Africa (RANA) has appointed Ghanaian media personality and public relations professional Matilda Mensah Marfo, popularly known as Tilly Akua Nipaa, as its Communications Director. The appointment, announced on Sunday, November 1, 2026, is aimed at strengthening the organisation's institutional communications, expanding public engagement and making human rights advocacy more accessible to citizens across Ghana and the African continent. Tilly Akua Nipaa has built a career in broadcasting, corporate communications, media relations, brand storytelling and stakeholder engagement. She has worked as a broadcaster and panellist on platforms under Despite Media and the Multimedia Group. She currently serves as Head of Public Relations and Marketing at Crux Global, where she leads the company's strategic communications and marketing initiatives.

results.title: Nigeria reports two suspected Ebola cases in northeast region
results.content: Health authorities in Nigeria are investigating two suspected Ebola cases in ​the country's northeast region, the Nigeria Centre for Disease ‌Control and Prevention said on Saturday.
